issues.legal_issue: The statutory undertaking to provide community buildings does not itself prohibit a colonizer from transferring land reserved for those buildings.
material_facts: The colonizer held licences to develop a colony in which sites were reserved for schools, hospitals, community centres and other community buildings.
The colonizer transferred interests in some reserved sites, and the transferees proposed to use the sites for the community purposes for which they had been reserved.
The governing undertaking allowed the colonizer either to construct the buildings itself or to have another institution or individual construct them at that other party’s cost.
issues.conclusion: The Act did not impose an express or implied absolute prohibition on transferring the reserved sites, provided their required use remained subject to the applicable regulatory controls.
issues.legal_principle: Section 3(3)(a)(iv) of the Haryana Development and Regulation of Urban Areas Act, 1975, Rule 11(e) of the Haryana Development and Regulation of Urban Areas Rules, 1976, and the corresponding licence condition require the provision of community buildings but do not prohibit transfers of the sites. Section 7 addresses transfers of plots in a colony for which a licence has not been obtained, and does not create the asserted prohibition here. The right to transfer is incidental to ownership and cannot be curtailed without statutory authority; a regulatory statute governing land use should not be construed as restricting transfers that do not affect the required use. The Court distinguished the purposive interpretation in Charan Lal Sahu v. Union of India and considered the interpretive approaches in Shamarao V. Parulekar v. District Magistrate, Ajaib Singh v. State of Punjab, and Tirath Singh v. Bachittar Singh; it also applied the principle that expropriatory statutes are strictly construed.

rule.if: licensed_colony_development and reserved_community_site and transfer_preserves_required_use and appeal_from_rejection_of_transfer_challenge

predicates.licensed_colony_development: A developer held a licence to develop a colony.
predicates.reserved_community_site: The land transferred was reserved for a school, hospital, community centre, or other community building.
predicates.transfer_preserves_required_use: The proposed transfer does not prevent the land from being used for its reserved community purpose.
predicates.appeal_from_rejection_of_transfer_challe: The proceeding is an appeal challenging the rejection of a claim that a transfer of reserved community land is permitted.

issues.definition: When a licensed developer transfers land reserved for a community purpose without changing that purpose, the transfer is not barred by the statutory undertaking alone.

issues.legal_issue: An executive instruction cannot impose a restriction on transferring land that the governing statute does not impose.
material_facts: The authorities issued instructions restricting the creation of further interests in community sites and applying conditions to earlier transfers.
The statute and licence contained no express restriction on transferring the sites.
The authorities had previously recognized transfers and approved building plans concerning some of the sites.
issues.conclusion: The executive instructions could not lawfully curtail the owners’ right to transfer the land, and the impugned judgment upholding them could not stand.
issues.legal_principle: Article 300A of the Constitution protects the ownership right to transfer property from being taken away except by authority of law. Section 3(3)(a)(iv) of the Haryana Development and Regulation of Urban Areas Act, 1975, does not expressly restrict transfer, and the Court found no basis to imply such a restriction. The Court also noted that a draft amendment proposing a prior-permission condition showed that such a condition had not previously existed. A statutory restriction cannot be created by executive fiat.

predicates.appeal_from_rejection_of_transfer_challe: The proceeding is an appeal challenging the rejection of a claim that a transfer of reserved community land is permitted.
predicates.executive_instruction_restricts_transfer: An administrative instruction imposes or purports to impose a restriction on transferring land.
predicates.no_enacted_transfer_restriction: No applicable enacted law imposes the transfer restriction asserted by the instruction.

issues.definition: If an administrative instruction restricts transfers without a corresponding restriction in enacted law, the instruction cannot validly impose that restriction.

issues.legal_issue: A transferee claiming through a licensed developer remains subject to the statutory and licence obligations governing the land’s use.
material_facts: The sites were transferred by a developer that held a licence subject to obligations concerning community buildings.
The transferees claimed their interests through the licensed developer.
The intended use of the sites remained the provision of community buildings, and the transferees undertook to comply with the applicable licence conditions and regulatory requirements.
issues.conclusion: The transfers did not remove the authorities’ control over the land’s use; the transferees remained bound by the applicable obligations, and lawful enforcement action remained available if those obligations were not met.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 3(3)(a)(iv) of the Haryana Development and Regulation of Urban Areas Act, 1975, and the corresponding rules and licence conditions, a transferee cannot acquire a greater right than the transferor possessed. The statutory obligations concerning the reserved use of the land continue through the transferee. Section 10 provides for consequences where the relevant obligations are not fulfilled, and the authorities may take action permitted by law, including taking over land where the community facilities have not been developed.

predicates.transferee_claims_through_licensed_devel: A person obtains an interest in land from a developer holding a licence subject to land-use obligations.
predicates.land_use_obligation_continues: The obligation governing the land’s required use remains applicable after the transfer.
predicates.community_use_is_regulated: The land is reserved for a community purpose subject to continuing regulatory control.

issues.definition: A transferee who claims through a licensed developer remains bound by the continuing obligation to use the land for its regulated purpose.

issues.legal_issue: The construction-cost undertaking distinguishes between construction by the colonizer and construction by another institution or individual.
material_facts: The statutory undertaking used the phrase “at his own cost” for construction by the colonizer and “at its cost” for construction by another institution or individual.
The Court considered whether the colonizer must bear the cost even when another institution or individual undertakes the construction.
issues.conclusion: The phrases have distinct meanings: the colonizer bears the cost when it constructs, while the other institution or individual bears the cost when it undertakes the construction.
issues.legal_principle: Section 3(3)(a)(iv) of the Haryana Development and Regulation of Urban Areas Act, 1975, uses different language for construction by the licensee and construction by another institution or individual. The corresponding Rule 11(e) and licence condition do not make those phrases synonymous. The Court applied the principle that different language used by the legislature is presumed to convey different meanings.

predicates.construction_obligation_allows_other_bui: The governing undertaking permits the licensed developer to have another institution or individual construct the required community building.
predicates.another_institution_or_individual_constr: An institution or individual other than the licensed developer undertakes the construction.

issues.definition: When another institution or individual undertakes construction under an obligation that permits it, that builder bears the construction cost.

issues.legal_issue: A bona fide transferee’s interest cannot be jeopardized by executive instructions absent a clear lack of transfer rights or evidence of fraud or collusion.
material_facts: The transferees acquired interests for valuable consideration after making inquiries into title.
The proposed transfers had been publicly advertised, and the authorities had not objected before issuing the later instructions.
The authorities did not plead that the developer had practised fraud or that the parties had colluded to achieve an illegal purpose.
The Court found no statutory bar that clearly deprived the developer of the right to transfer the sites.
issues.conclusion: The transferees’ interests could not be jeopardized by the executive instructions in the circumstances of the case.
issues.legal_principle: A bona fide transferee for value who has exercised due diligence is not deprived of an acquired interest merely by executive instructions where the governing law does not clearly prohibit the transfer. The Court qualified this protection where it is readily apparent that the transferor had no right to transfer and the transfer would be illegal, or where fraud or collusion is established. The principle was applied alongside the Court’s conclusions on Section 3(3)(a)(iv) of the Haryana Development and Regulation of Urban Areas Act, 1975, and Article 300A of the Constitution.

rule.if: bona_fide_purchase_for_value and due_diligence_exercised and executive_instruction_jeopardizes_interest and no_clear_transfer_bar and no_fraud_or_collusion_established

predicates.bona_fide_purchase_for_value: A transferee acquired the interest honestly and for valuable consideration.
predicates.due_diligence_exercised: The transferee made reasonable inquiries before acquiring the interest.
predicates.executive_instruction_jeopardizes_intere: An executive instruction is used to put the acquired interest at risk.
predicates.no_clear_transfer_bar: The governing law does not clearly establish that the transferor lacked the right to transfer or that the transfer was illegal.
predicates.no_fraud_or_collusion_established: Fraud or collusion by the transferor and transferee has not been established.

issues.definition: A diligent bona fide purchaser for value is protected from having an interest jeopardized by executive instruction when no clear transfer bar, fraud, or collusion is established.
